# Teacher onboarding canonical actions (S2)

The canonical assistant-UI action path is persisted as a frozen receipt mode
(`legacy` or `canonical`) in migration 018. A canonical receipt validates the
exact Dialog-owned assistant-UI source and computes the message body and source
UI digest in Teacher. It then sends one exact-token internal Dialog command:

`identity (receipt -> correlation/causation, source interaction evidence) -> canonical_body`

Dialog materializes one ordinary Student message and returns its message ID;
Teacher records that ID as the terminal `materialized` receipt. This path does
not call Student, AI Prompt, proactive Dialog delivery, or the generic Teacher
worker. A timeout is retried with the same canonical command ID; it never falls
back to legacy after a receipt has been claimed.

The public action request remains IDs-only. The legacy v1 response and behavior
are unchanged. Canonical responses use the strict `assistant-ui-action-result.v2`
contract and are dark by default. `TEACHER_ONBOARDING_CANONICAL_ACTIONS_ENABLED`
requires `TEACHER_UNIFIED_COORDINATOR_ENABLED`, and the current runtime keeps
both flags false by default. S5 now composes that coordinator:
canonical mode cannot be enabled alone, and unified coordination additionally
requires dense Dialog ordering. While unified coordination is disabled, the
worker still blocks action-receipt jobs before context, Student, or LLM work.

For a policy-v2 prompt, the action result still means only that Dialog
materialized the canonical Student message. It is pending the ordinary dense
turn that applies the Student effect and resolves readiness; the result does
not claim that the draft, path, course, or lesson is complete. Migration 020
also fences a new canonical claim against the exact active prompt before any
Dialog or Student effect. An already materialized exact receipt remains a safe
replay after the prompt has closed.

Migration 018 down is fail-closed whenever canonical evidence exists. It must
not be used to erase a materialized message ledger.
